text: In this town, there is an old oak tree. And inside it, I found a map.
It said: find three things, and you will know me.
Thing number one: a cap. At the very top of the clock tower.
I climbed all two hundred stairs. The wind tried to take it. I said: no way.
Thing number two: a fishing rod, by the pond.
A duck had it. The duck did not want to give it back.
We ran three laps around the pond. The duck won. But then, he gave it back anyway.
Thing number three: a recipe book, at the bakery.
On the first page, in big letters, it said: pancakes for my son.
The last line of the map pointed to a tree house I had never noticed before.
Inside, there was a box. And in the box, there was a photo.
A man, holding a tiny baby. The baby had my ears.
And there was a letter.
If you are reading this, you are big now. I can't be there with you.
But I left you my cap, my fishing rod, and our pancakes.
Every time you make them, I'm right there with you. Love, Dad.
I read it three times. Then I went home.
That night, I made pancakes for Mom. They were a little burned. She said they were perfect.
I put one more plate on the table. And his cap, right next to it.
Then I looked out the window. And one star winked at me.
